item.subject: science
item.stem:
The teacher writes one answer on the board: "four". Arjun must invent a curious situation and a scientific question that this answer could fit. Ideas mentioned include ice cubes melting, ant trails on sugar, and bouncing balls.

Which response best follows the activity?

options.A: He imagines four ice cubes melting at different speeds and asks which factors could explain the differences.
options.B: He asks, "Why do ants follow sugar trails?" without checking whether "four" answers that question.
options.C: He says a scientific question is valid only when its answer is already known, so the activity is impossible.
options.D: He writes any long, dramatic question about bouncing balls and says it is valid because it sounds creative, even though "four" does not answer it.
